name: Corc mac Luigthic
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Corc mac Luigthic is an Irish hero and king. He took possession of the throne at Cashel in Munster. His fairy mother, Fedelm, presided over the investment there. The rite left his ear singed red through magic. He sailed to Scotland for an audience with the Pict monarch. A rival had stamped Ogham words on his shield that condemned him to die. An ally reframed the writing as a welcome, so Corc wed the king's daughter and set up an Irish dynasty.

okr.objective: Corc mac Luigthic is a heroic king of Cashel.
key_results: He was made king at Cashel in Munster.
His ear was magically singed red at the rite.
An ally rescued him from a death plot in Scotland.
He wed the king daughter and founded a line.
